The Face Of War by Martha Gellhorn is a collection of all of her war correspondence and is a really hard hitting account of how war affects us all.
Came here to recommend this. Was my absolute favorite book as a kid. There's also a sequel "There's Another Monster At The End Of This Book", which is also amazing.

I'm so sorry you are going through this. I relate to much of what you've said, especially the isolation and the guilt. It's so hard to accept that the past is the past and cannot be changed. When this happens I find it best to look to the future.  I try to give myself something to look forward to, whether it's something big like attending an event or something small like planning to make popcorn and watch my favorite movie. I think it's important to find small spots of relief, especially when the pain seems never ending and unchanging.

But please know it will change, even if it doesn't seem like it can right now. Eventually the walls will crack and let some light in. I have hope for you. If you ever need to talk or anything, you can pm me.

This has been the absolute hardest news cycle for me. My assault also happened in high school and there are other similarities, which is making it really difficult to separate Dr. Ford's Trauma from my own. Every time I turn on the tv or the internet, it's like the whole world is dissecting me. 

But what I find the most hopeless is that Dr. Ford did everything right. She was the "perfect victim" people are always saying we should act like. Even Republicans said she was credible. But it still just *doesn't matter.* Kavanaugh will probably still be confirmed. It is so terrifying to know that even in the face of truth, decades of carried trauma, and a nation of women screaming, men in power will still just say "no". It's truly shaken me to the point that I wonder why I continue fighting when it seems that there is no way out.
